theoph_1cmt_foa.estimation_note: Standard two-stage estimation: each subject fitted independently, then the individual estimates summarised. This is NOT non-linear mixed-effects estimation. Two-stage is known to overestimate between-subject variability, especially with sparse sampling, because each individual estimate carries its own estimation error into the variance calculation. The reported CV% is therefore an upper bound on true between-subject variability.
theoph_1cmt_foa.interpretation: On held-out subjects the model's absolute average fold error is 1.293 and its average fold error is 1.209, so typical precision is about 29% with over-prediction bias of 21%. 90% of held-out observations fall within 2-fold of prediction. Median absolute percent error is 19% (RMSE 1.503 mg/L). This is evidence only for the population and study design this dataset covers: twelve subjects each given a single oral dose of theophylline, with plasma concentrations measured at 11 time points over roughly 25 hours. It is not evidence of accuracy in any other population, route, dose range or disease state, and it is not clinical validation.
